verdicts.law: A5 / the four-faces rule (never a paraphrase of a sibling; the faces differ in CONSTRUCTION, not vocabulary alone) + entailment item 4 + C7

(a) Against face 0 this is one clause in nominal dress, not a second construction: the same read order (R2 then R1), the same verb 'is entered', the same lexis 'provided/provision against beasts', and the same landing ('as quiet' / 'is a quiet one'); the subject is the only one of the three axes that moves, and the words themselves do not move at all, so the pair does not clear A5's 'past a synonym swap' bar. verdicts.cure: Reverse the read order and re-land the face so it is not face 0 recast, naming the referent in the same stroke, e.g. 'Beasts come to little in the country around {settlement}, and provision against them is entered at the town.' The nominal compression (the variant's density floor, skeleton 2.6) is kept, the order, the subject and the landing noun all move, the referent is named, and no claim is added.

readAloud: Variant 1 [ledger]: the variant lands well aloud and its two-sentence shape earns the second sentence every time; the parent's 'A force stands behind the works' is the firmest close in the pool. Face 1-b is the set's heaviest at twenty-five words and its closing clause thuds on the repeated noun where the first sentence has already done the work; face 1-c's 'A force is entered' is the one opening in the pool that sounds unmistakably like an office speaking, which is what the tag is for.

Variant 2 [street]: face 2-a's 'is up' is the freshest phrase in the pool and the only one that sounds like a town saying it rather than a record stating it; face 2-c's 'The muster stands with the works' has the best opening rhythm of the twelve. Face 2-b is where the ear catches the fault already named: spoken aloud it comes out as a proverb, and the tune gives the maxim away before the law does.

Variant 3 [counterforce]: face 3-b's outside/inside pair is the cleanest read-aloud in the set and needs nothing. The parent's fronted 'Against frontier country' is the strongest-sounding line of the twelve, which is exactly why its unlicensed word is worth naming; the cure costs the sentence very little of that weight. Face 3-c trails past its anchor when spoken: the voice reaches 'and with it' and has nothing to hold, which is the binding fault heard rather than parsed.

verdicts.finding: States C1, C2 and C3 in the ledger's own plain entry with no record noun and no citation (W24). 'the town's works' seats the possessive on the TOWN (W1); 'behind the works' is the key's own conjunction, not a spatial or manning fact; the second sentence carries 'the works' forward (R-i at k = 0) and closes on an OBJECT. No breach found on the card, the bars W1-W27, the label traps or the hard walls.

verdicts.law: W14 (a label at its ENGINE meaning, never its dictionary sense), read against the skeleton's fence 1 AND the skeleton's own section 0.2 (this branch's product chrome is not a licence for the same words in a face); A6 as the consequence
verdicts.quote: The works at {settlement} sit on an active frontier
verdicts.finding: 'active' is not in the entailment table's engine reading of frontier (L-2 gives the middle exposure tier and the unmeasured-town default, and no activity of any kind). Its only two supports are product-chrome surfaces (SummaryTab.jsx:37, threatAssessment.js:74), and the skeleton's section 0.2 rules that exactly this branch's chrome is not a licence for the same words in a face. If 'active' carries anything past the tier token, this face is not claim-equal to its three siblings, which all say 'frontier country' (A6 reads across the faces). Unproven at this desk either way: the marker recorded it as fence 1, an OPEN ROW for the chair, and a refuter cannot settle a chair's open row, so the verdict is WITHHELD rather than FAIL. Recorded as a secondary risk and NOT as a finding: seating THE WORKS as the subject of 'sit on a frontier' leans the word toward the border reading L-2 refuses (the tier is exposure, not a boundary), where the shipped line seated the settlement.
verdicts.cure: Only if the chair rules the bare tier word licensed: 'The works at {settlement} stand in frontier country.' The declared construction, the limb order C2 to C1 to C3, the slot set and the inverted second sentence are untouched. The cost is the pool's one shipped turn kept under 21.4, and that trade is the chair's, not the curer's.

verdicts.finding: States C2 in the office's own formula ('carried as standing', R-vi/W7, a licensed surface with no record noun and no citation), C3 as an elliptical conjunct with 'them' binding to the works, and C1. 'At the town of {settlement}' is W5's naming form. The second sentence carries 'the town' forward (R-i) and closes on a CONDITION. The agentless passive is the form the referent table lists at the RIGHT layer. No breach found.

Then C1, then C2 by W15's second always-safe spelling ('what the town has built'). Carries 'the force' forward and closes on an OBJECT. Distinct from face 2 in subject, limb order, formula surface and close, so the two formula faces are not paraphrases (A5). No breach found.

States C1, C2 and C3 with no slot, as the parent's empty set requires. The street's licensed form here is to state the standing PLAINLY, because no field holds what the town says or thinks (R-iii, R-DA-13's belief-frame floor), and this face does exactly that: no attitude, no duration, no grade, no fused agent (W23). 'inside it' binds to 'the town', which has an outside on every member of the walls bucket, and not to the works, which would assert the circuit D-3 places in NOT ENTAILED. Closes on an OBJECT. No breach found.

States C2 in the street's plainest idiom ('is up' is presence; it asserts no height, material, gate or manning, and stays true of a Citadel and of Gates (if walled) alike because the class word carries it), then C3, then C1. 'with it' binds to 'what the town has built', the immediately preceding noun phrase. Hands 'frontier country' forward to the two modifier positions (k = 2). No breach found.

verdicts.law: W5 (the naming-form article: a frame that needs the generic article to carry a band is a MAXIM frame; state the band as a band) and R-DA-12 (the generalisation test)
verdicts.quote: In frontier country the town has a force
verdicts.finding: The fronted bare-noun tier with no article, joined to a generic-looking definite subject and a habitual 'has', reads as a life-general claim about frontier towns rather than a standing fact of THIS town: the maxim frame W5 names and the generalisation R-DA-12 tests for. The card licenses the row only as a STANDING fact of the record; a maxim is a claim over a class the card does not reach, and W2 requires the tier to be stated over this town's country. The three reads are all present and the rest of the face is sound. The fault is the frame, not the content.
verdicts.cure: Anchor the country to this town's own outside, adding no claim: 'In the frontier country outside, the town has a force, and that force stands behind the works.' The limb order C1 to C3 to C2, the resumptive 'that force', the close on 'the works' (an OBJECT) and the empty slot set are all kept.

verdicts.finding: States C3 by the force's second always-safe class word ('the muster', ADDENDUM 13 A.5 as O-2 re-cut it), and this is the one pool where that word is safest: the force limb is garrison OR militia and EXCLUDES the watch, so A-11's watch-only-town objection cannot arise. It is the CLASS word and not the record, so W24, W7 and OV-5 are clear (no roll, no rolls, no books). Then C2, then C1 by the engine's own bare token ('is frontier'), which the adjacent pool of this same block already carries. 'beyond the town' is seated on the TOWN and not the works, the enclosure breach cured. Closes on a CONDITION. No breach found.

verdicts.law: the card's may NOT: a cause (a purpose predicated of the works toward the country); the skeleton's fence 3 (the counterforce sets the two sides down and settles neither, the reader draws the deterrence); ADDENDUM 8 ruling 2 as the skeleton generalises it (a block's or a key's own name is its name, not a licence)
verdicts.quote: Against frontier country the town of {settlement} has its works standing
verdicts.finding: 'Against' asserts WHY the works stand, an orientation of the works toward the tier that no field on this card computes. The card prints 'relation: (a spine takes no relation)' and refuses a cause outright; the key's own tail 'credible deterrence' is expressly not a licence (skeleton 0.2); and the block's subtitle ('what the town actually has standing against each'), which the draft leaned on, is the corpus's own prose and not a typed field, so it cannot license the word either. This is the weakened survivor of the shipped v3's cause clause ('and the reason is that...') that the rewrite exists to drop. The pool's other three counterforce faces set the pressure beside what stands in it WITHOUT asserting the relation, which is the proof the stance does not need the word.
verdicts.cure: State the pressure as position rather than opposition, one word: 'In frontier country the town of {settlement} has its works standing, and behind them a force.' The fronted pressure, the elliptical second conjunct, the slot, the limb order C1 to C2 to C3 and the close on 'a force' all stand, and the shipped backing conjunction ('and a force behind it', re-seated on the works per W1) is kept intact as 21.4's floor.

verdicts.finding: States C2, then C3 as the pool's ONE negated surface on a PRESENT read, never the opener and one per variant (W10 / R-ii), then C1. The litotes sits squarely inside the counterforce's stance (the absence read against what the tier would lead one to expect) and rejects no alternative, so it is not a contrast needing a named sibling (R-DA-02). 'the country outside' carries no pronoun to mis-bind, the enclosure breach cured. Closes on a CONDITION. No breach found.

The cleanest realisation of the stance in the set: C1 as the pressure, then C3 and C2 as what stands, juxtaposed with no relation asserted between them. The outside/inside pair is seated on THE TOWN, which has both on any member of the walls bucket, so it asserts no circuit, no line and no enclosure of the works (D-6, D-3). Closes on an OBJECT where its siblings close on a condition and on a name not given. No breach found.

verdicts.law: W1 (the binding rule, as this round's own LOCATIVE AUDIT applied it at 3-a and 2-c); W23 (no relation between two referents that no field computes); Part B 21.2 (a refinement keeps its ground only while it stays lawful)
verdicts.quote: and with it what the town has built
verdicts.finding: The elliptical conjunct's 'it' has no reachable anchor. The intended antecedent is 'the town's force', eight words and two noun phrases back; the nearest candidates are '{settlement}' and 'the frontier country'. On the nearest reading the face says what the town has built stands WITH THE COUNTRY, a relation the card computes nowhere and W23 refuses. This is not unclarity standing alone: on its most available reading the sentence carries a relation no field holds. It is also a regression the REFINEMENT introduced, and 21.2's own test catches it, because the draft's face carried no pronoun at all ('In the frontier country around {settlement} the town's force stands with what the town has built') and was re-cut only to move a limb-order figure.
verdicts.cure: Give the conjunct a reachable anchor, adding no claim: 'The town's force stands in the frontier country about {settlement}, and with that force what the town has built.' The demonstrative binds unambiguously; the elliptical conjunct, the set's one A-NAME-NOT-GIVEN close, the slot and the C3 to C1 to C2 order that separates this face from 3-b all survive.

readAloud: Variant 1 [ledger]: the four land as a record; face 0's long country phrase and face 2's office formula are the two that sound compiled rather than composed, and face 2 is the only one not leaning on a negative particle, so it is the one the ear keeps. Face 1's two clipped sentences give the pool its short end but the second starts cold on 'The place', and face 3's 'nothing of works or muster stands' catches the tongue where the rest of the variant runs clean. Three of the four close on an absence, and with 'force' gone from every face the ear hears 'muster' four times across the variant's landings.

Variant 2 [street]: faces 0 and 1 sound like a place talking about itself; faces 2 and 3 sound like the ledger's variant with different nouns. Face 2 trails off on its apposition and has no verb to land on, which is audible — the sentence stops rather than closes. Face 3 opens on the same beat as variant 1's fourth face, so a reader meeting both towns would hear the template before the fact.

Variant 3 [visitor]: the strongest variant of the three by ear — four different ways of noticing (coming, seeing, finding, meeting), no interior and no verdict anywhere, and face 2's turn outward at the end is the one sentence in the pool that reads like a passage rather than an entry. Face 3's 'and the next is' is the weakest beat, and weaker now than in the draft because its tail repeats face 1's.

verdicts.law: THE DENSITY FLOOR (Part B 21.4, read against the SHIPPED sentence) with the skeleton 1.5 'turns worth keeping' and 1.7 'a lost lawful turn'
verdicts.quote: the place stands inside it without works or muster
verdicts.finding: The shipped row's lawful clause 'no force' — the engine's own token at defenseStateProse.js:655, which the skeleton lists as a turn a face may carry whole and whose vanishing FROM THE WHOLE VARIANT it names as the regression ('the ledger's variant is where the engine's own words for the reads belong') — is gone from all four faces of variant 1. verdicts.law: R-i (ADDENDUM 12: a spine's own second sentence carries a noun forward from its first regardless of k) and THE THREAD (owner, 2026-09-08)

Unproven; flagged for the chair.

The sibling shape the refinement cites as warrant is 'nothing of the muster holds them', a definite NP; the bare-plural version reads more mannered, and the refinement replaced one mannered member of the variant (a cleft) with another. Unproven: it sits at the edge of the plain register rather than demonstrably outside it, and it buys the variant its ONLY object close (R-DA-04's varied close kind), which a plainer rewrite would spend.

verdicts.quote: In a country plagued with monsters, {settlement} stands open and unmustered
verdicts.finding: The whole keyed condition in one predicate (grammar V1, the variant's declared construction under W4); the place as subject in the street's own plain shape; C2 and C3 in the compressed positive pair that 21.4's density law protects from being made plainer. Eleven words, the pool's short end after 2.1.

verdicts.quote: Out in monster country {settlement} keeps neither works nor muster

verdicts.quote: Walls at {settlement} with townspeople behind them, a part-time force
verdicts.finding: Clean. The shipped clause stands verbatim as the variant's density floor (§21.4, ADDENDUM 6); the appositive names what the force is at D-8's definitional grain and adds no claim; the force noun is the BARE plural, so the co-extension of finding A is not reached; 'its' binds to 'a part-time force' (W1); the garrison's absence is carried by what the militia IS, never by its noun (W12, the card's force-class line T-F12).

verdicts.law: §21.4 THE DENSITY LAW (the refinement regression), read with MOVE-GRAMMAR §1.4.1 THE THREAD and the register card's licensed recurrence
verdicts.quote: has walls, and the militia is part-time, drawn from the townspeople
verdicts.finding: The refinement struck 'behind them' and put nothing in its place. This is the pool's ONE face whose two licensed reads are joined by a bare 'and' with no relational carrier; the four other faces that lost the idiom each kept one ('with them' x3, 'and so are' x1). The key is ONE condition — walls true AND militia true read together (R-v) — and the backing idiom is what states it as one. The law named for the cut is R-DA-05 / A11 spread, but the refine's own reserve row records that the gate owns no ceiling on a licensed preposition — a judgment, not a measurement — while §1.4.1 rules A11's echo bound counts FACTS, not nouns, and the register card licenses a word that recurs. A lawful compression was made plainer with no law behind the change. It also leaves 'the militia' an unbound definite on the SPINE, the first thing a reader of the composed passage meets.
verdicts.cure: Restore a relational carrier on the second clause without restoring a claim — 'and the militia with them is part-time, drawn from the townspeople' (the pool's own 'with them'), or the draft's 'behind them'. The refinement's lawful gain ('the militia' for 'the muster', R-DA-10's noun spread) is kept either way.

verdicts.law: ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with entailment D-1 / D-3 ('who built it', 'who paid' NOT ENTAILED) against D-6's ratified generic
verdicts.quote: and so are the walls the town has built
verdicts.finding: The restrictive relative predicates the BUILDING of the walls of the town. D-6 ratifies the free relative 'what the town has built' as an always-safe generic true of every walls-bucket member; D-1 and D-3 both list 'who built it' and 'who paid' under NOT ENTAILED for the members this key actually renders (the hamlet/village Palisade or earthworks). The table contradicts itself on the point and the chair has not ruled, so the face is UNPROVEN, not refuted. Everything else holds: 'carried standing' carried across by the ellipsis is the office's own formula (R-vi / W7), no record noun and no citation appear (W24), and the indefinite head 'A part-time muster of the townspeople' does not equate the class with the force.
verdicts.cure: Take D-6's ratified form verbatim — 'and so is what the town has built' — or 'and so are the works'; the ellipsis, the formula and the force-then-works order are untouched.

verdicts.law: the licence card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'; 'an exemption from a duty', whoIsExempt null everywhere), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with entailment D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: the force entered with them is the townspeople, part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A: a definite plural 'the townspeople' in an equative with 'the force' asserts that the force and the town's people are ONE SET. The recorded rows restrict the militia to a subset — 'Able-bodied residents drill and muster' (institutionalCatalog.js:338), 'Fit residents train and turn out' / 'The able-bodied drill together' (institutionDescVariants.js:442-443), 'A community drawn up for its own defence' (:1158) — and the only row carrying a totality, 'All able-bodied citizens obligated to defend town' (:1344), is the TOWN row, which never generates natively (R-A). D-8 licenses 'townspeople' as what the force is MADE OF, never as who all of them are.
verdicts.cure: Break the co-extension without adding a claim: drop the article — 'and the force entered with them is townspeople, part-time' (the shipped clause's own bare-plural form).

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'; 'an exemption from a duty'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2 — aggravated by the intensifier
verdicts.quote: The force behind the walls is the townspeople themselves
verdicts.finding: Finding A at its sharpest: 'themselves' forecloses the partitive reading entirely and makes the identification exclusive — the force IS the town's people, all of them, which the recorded rows (able-bodied / fit residents / a community) and whoIsExempt being null both refuse. This is the variant's numbered line, so the breach sits on the face a falsy seed and the canonical projection draw.
verdicts.cure: 'The force behind the walls is drawn from the townspeople, a part-time muster that turns out off its own work' — the partitive is D-8's own relation ('raised'), costs no claim, and keeps 'turn out', the pool's one shipped compression.

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: what turns out behind them is the townspeople, part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A in a specificational pseudo-cleft: the set that turns out is identified AS the townspeople, so the class and the force are again co-extensive over a bounded, specific set.
verdicts.cure: Drop the article — 'and what turns out behind them is townspeople, part-time'; the free relative, 'behind them' (load-bearing here against the ordinary English of 'turns out to be') and the landing all stand.

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: The townspeople turn out part-time behind the town's walls.
verdicts.finding: Finding A with the definite class as the AGENT of the force's own act: every townsperson turns out. The engine's own surface at this key is a restricted bare plural ('Fit residents train and turn out', institutionDescVariants.js:442), and this face keeps the act while dropping the restriction and adding the article.
verdicts.cure: Drop the article — 'Townspeople turn out part-time behind the town's walls.' Nine words, no comma, both reads, the possessor still seated on the town.

verdicts.quote: The townspeople in it turn out and go back to their own work.
verdicts.finding: Clean. 'in it' restricts the plural to those on the muster, so finding A is not reached; 'it' carries the muster forward at k = 0 (R-i); the second sentence states D-8's own 'raising them takes them off other work' rather than glossing the first (W6); 'their' binds to 'The townspeople' (W1); the fronted locative is the declared construction (W4).

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: the town's force with them is the townspeople, raised part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A in an equative. The shipped line's one lawful property (the possessive frame, the two-step order) and the compression 'raised part-time off their own work' are sound; the co-extension of the force with the whole class is the single fault.
verdicts.cure: Drop the article — 'and the town's force with them is townspeople, raised part-time off their own work'; nothing else moves.

verdicts.quote: and behind them is a force of the townspeople. It is part-time
verdicts.finding: Clean. The indefinite head 'a force' keeps the phrase partitive, so finding A is not reached; the pool's one lawful inversion; 'It' carries the force forward at k = 0 (R-i); the standing condition lands last, as R-iv's OPEN is construed on this settled key (skeleton fence 3); 'its' binds to 'a force' (W1).

verdicts.law: the card's REFUSED COLUMNS ('a totality over persons'), ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 with D-8, and W2
verdicts.quote: the townspeople behind them are the town's force, raised part-time
verdicts.finding: Finding A with the definite class as the SUBJECT of the equative — the town's people ARE the town's force. Secondary, and not the ground of this verdict: with face 0 this face runs the same frame in reverse (a walls clause, an equative joining force and townspeople, a part-time landing), which is close to the edge of ADDENDUM 7 rule 4 / W4's construction distance.
verdicts.cure: Put the force on the subject and the bare plural in the predicate — 'and the force behind them is townspeople, raised part-time'; this also widens the distance from face 0, which keeps the townspeople in the predicate.

verdicts.quote: That force is a militia of the townspeople, part-time.
verdicts.finding: Clean. The indefinite head keeps the phrase partitive; 'That force' carries the noun forward at k = 0 (R-i); 'a militia' is licensed outright here (the read IS forces.militia.present, referent table 2.1); the second sentence adds the recorded name and the composition rather than restating the first (W6); the condition lands last.

readAloud: Variant 1 [ledger]: the verbless entry lands, and the office's formula carries faces 2 and 3 — 'and so are' is the sharpest joint in the pool, the whole of the second entry done in three words. Face 1 is the flattest line of the twelve to the ear: two facts set side by side with nothing between them, and a definite 'the militia' arriving with no one having said the town has one.

Variant 2 [street]: 'turn out' carries every face, and read in sequence three of them put the townspeople and the turning-out in the same order, so the four sound closer than their word counts suggest. The nine-word face is the best line in the pool aloud — it lands where it stops.

Variant 3 [unfolding]: the two-step order reads cleanly and the condition lands last on all four, which gives the variant one shape and one cadence. Face 1's inversion is the only line in the pool that sounds spoken rather than filed. Face 3 is the longest of the twelve and its second sentence opens on 'That force', which reads like a clerk going back to make himself plain.

Variant 1 [ledger]: read aloud, three of the four faces land on the idiom rather than the place - "answers a raid on its own ground" comes off the tongue as meets them where it has the advantage; face 2's "turn out on their own ground" is the one that lands as a place, and face 0 runs out of breath on its third adjunct.

Variant 2 [street]: the variant reads as one movement (who turns out, what it costs them, what there is to hold) and that movement is its strength; but three of the four faces open on a person-plural subject and two end on the same ten words, so read in sequence the family flattens into one sentence said four times.

Variant 3 [visitor]: the four openings are genuinely four (finds, sees, comes upon, passes) and the eye stays an eye; the second sentence is the same cadence four times over ("is part-time, not a professional garrison"), so the variant's last beat is where a reader would first hear the machine.

verdicts.law: R-DA-03 (the qualification gets its own sentence, never a tail, never a third); the register card's "a qualification is a sentence, never a tail"
verdicts.quote: on its own ground, in place of a professional garrison, with nothing
verdicts.finding: Three adjuncts hang off one verb and R1 arrives as the third of them; "for it to stand behind" then seats "it" one word after "the town", so the capability clause can bind to the town rather than to the muster. The variant also realises the [ledger] stance in none of its four faces (R-vi's office formula appears nowhere, while all five sibling Invasion & War pools realise theirs with it).
verdicts.cure: Cut R1 into its own sentence carrying a noun forward from the first: "A citizen militia at {settlement} answers a raid on its own ground, in place of a professional garrison. Around the town nothing is built for that muster to stand behind."

verdicts.law: R-DA-02 (a civic LACK is the first half only, stated flat, no completing contrast), with R-DA-03
verdicts.quote: answers a raid on its own ground with no wall around the town
verdicts.finding: R1 rides as a circumstantial on the capability clause, so the lack reads as the completing half of a contrast ("it answers a raid, but without a wall") - the shipped line's "counts for something against a raid" balance restored in another dress. Beside "answers a raid" the idiom "on its own ground" also pulls toward the advantage sense the skeleton licenses only as a place (D-8 NOT ENTAILED: competence).
verdicts.cure: Give R1 its own flat sentence and leave the raid clause unqualified: "...and it answers a raid on its own ground. No wall stands around the town."

verdicts.law: W6 (no doubled beat: a clause that restates the read it follows is the summarising beat)
verdicts.quote: Those citizens stand with nothing built around the town.
verdicts.finding: The second sentence's subject clause restates the presence the first sentence already stated ("the citizens of {settlement} turn out on their own ground"); the beat exists only to carry R1, which is the summarising beat W6 refuses.
verdicts.cure: Drop the restating clause and carry the noun forward inside the lack itself: "Around the town nothing is built for that muster to stand behind."

verdicts.law: the licence card's may NOT ("another civic object of the class force"; "a future"); W25; R-DA-02
verdicts.quote: answers a raid on their own ground, not a professional garrison
verdicts.finding: The contrast is seated on "answers a raid", so the plain reading is that the muster answers a raid and not a professional garrison - the engagement claim the rewrite exists to drop, restored by attachment rather than by wording. The face is also face 0's construction with two synonyms swapped: same subject class, same order of reads (R2, raid, R3, R1) and same landing (A5, the four-faces rule).
verdicts.cure: Seat the contrast on the muster and re-cut the construction: "Citizens of {settlement}, not a professional garrison, make the muster that answers a raid on their own ground."

verdicts.law: W1 (a pronoun after a clause binds to that clause's nearest object); the ambiguity that opens a claim after the spine
verdicts.quote: It comes off their own work, and nothing is built around
verdicts.finding: "It" has "a professional garrison" as its nearest antecedent and the town as its next; the muster it is meant to name is two clauses back, so the licensed entailment (raising them takes them off other work) is hung on the wrong referent.
verdicts.cure: Seat the people as the subject of the consequence: "They come to it off their own work, and nothing is built around the town for them to hold."

verdicts.law: A5 / the four-faces rule (the faces differ in construction - subject, order of the reads, landing noun - never in vocabulary alone)
verdicts.quote: Townspeople make the muster at {settlement}, part-time and in place of
verdicts.finding: Face 0's construction exactly: a person-plural subject plus "make the muster at {settlement}, part-time and [contrast]", then a work clause and an R1 tail, in the same read order and landing on the same noun. Only "The town's own people" to "Townspeople" and "not" to "in place of" move - a synonym swap, not a second construction.
verdicts.cure: Re-cut on a construction face 0 does not use, fronting the two entailments: "Part-time and off their own work, the townspeople of {settlement} make the muster instead of a professional garrison. The town has built nothing for them to hold."

verdicts.law: A5 / the four-faces rule; R-DA-05 (the pool is the unit of spread)
verdicts.quote: and nothing is built around the town for them to hold
verdicts.finding: The face closes on face 0's clause word for word, so two of the variant's four faces land on the same ten words; a face that repeats a sibling's clause verbatim is below a synonym swap, not above it.
verdicts.cure: Vary R1's surface on this face only: "...and the town has built nothing for that muster to hold."

verdicts.law: R-DA-03 (never a tail, never a third); R-DA-18 (the antique air lives in the noun, never in the syntax)
verdicts.quote: part-time and not a professional garrison, off their own work and with
verdicts.finding: One sentence carries four stacked adjuncts, and it does so after a cleft whose copula does not agree with its plural complement ("What turns out at {settlement} is townspeople"); the shape is costume in the syntax with the pool's heaviest tail pile behind it.
verdicts.cure: Break the sentence in two: state the muster and the contrast first, then the work and the lack - "Townspeople are what turns out at {settlement}, part-time and not a professional garrison. They come to it off their own work, with nothing built around the town for them to hold."

verdicts.quote: finds the town's own people at their work and no wall
verdicts.finding: R1, R2 and R3 are all stated; the stranger only finds and sees (W27); the thread is carried by "Those people"; the contrast is seated on the militia, not on a raid; the close is the sibling-licensed contrast in the one variant licensed to close on it (wall 5).

verdicts.quote: are what a stranger sees at {settlement}, and no wall stands
verdicts.finding: A construction of its own (the perceived object fronted), the lack stated flat, and the muster introduced with its antecedent in place ("The muster they make"); no unlicensed claim, no citation, no slot outside the bag.

verdicts.law: THE THREAD (MOVE-GRAMMAR §1.4.1; R-i: a spine's own second sentence carries a noun forward from its first); A5
verdicts.quote: That muster is part-time and not a professional garrison.
verdicts.finding: The demonstrative points at no antecedent - the first sentence names the town's own people, their work and the absent wall, and never a muster - so the second sentence hands nothing back. The clause is also face 1's second sentence with its subject swapped.
verdicts.cure: Supply the antecedent and change the construction with it: "They muster part-time, instead of a professional garrison."

verdicts.quote: are at their own work behind no wall
verdicts.finding: The pool's compressed face; "behind no wall" is the density floor's own compression and is not made plainer; "Their muster" binds to the people who are the sentence's subject (W1); the stranger only passes, which the skeleton names a safe verb.

readAloud: Variant 1: the four ledger faces spread their verbs as the skeleton asked (carries, are entered, is carried standing, stands) and the office's cadence is audible without a record noun anywhere. Face 3 is the shortest line in the pool and the ear likes it best, which is exactly why its collision with the twin's own opening line costs the most when a reader meets both on one page.

Variant 2: the shipped short line still lands better aloud than any of its three siblings, which is the density law's point. Face 1's doubled by-phrase reads well immediately after the spine and after a sibling modifier. Face 3 now reads as two flat clauses where the draft had one turn, and the ear hears 'here' and 'the place' as two names for one town inside nine words (R-DA-22's reverse thesaurus; reported, not a verdict).

Variant 3: the eye-verbs spread cleanly (sees, notices, comes upon, meets) and no face lets the stranger judge or be told. Face 2 has the cleanest thread in the pool (the slot carried forward as 'The town', the second sentence's own subject); face 3's reduced relative reads a beat slower than its siblings but holds.

verdicts.quote: {settlement} carries a standing force and no perimeter.
verdicts.finding: Both licensed reads on one verb with no joint - the pool's density floor kept at its compression, the unlicensed grade struck and replaced by the engine's own word for bucket presence. The ledger stance is carried by the office's word; no record noun and no citation (W24, A13). Slot carried once; opens the pool's one settlement-opening variant (wall 10).

verdicts.quote: are entered at {settlement}, and the town keeps no works
verdicts.finding: R1 at the person-plural class grain in the office's lawful formula (R-vi / W7 'entered', which is a standpoint surface and not a record noun), R2 on the wall class's always-safe generic (ENTAILMENT A-7) with the town seated as possessor (W1). One negated surface; closes on a civic noun of the key.

verdicts.quote: A force is carried standing at {settlement}
verdicts.finding: The landed same-page twin's ledger face 2 shares the surface 'carried standing at {settlement}', but that surface is the OFFICE'S OWN FORMULA, which the register card expressly licenses to recur ('Repeat the office's formula because it is the office's. The WORD may recur; the FACT must not'). The fact is differently built, the absence does not open the face (wall 3), and the thread carries the slot forward as 'the town' (R-i at k = 0).

verdicts.law: A11 sibling distance / the same-page C7; the register card ('the WORD may recur; the FACT must not'); aggravated by Part B 21.4 the density law
verdicts.quote: The muster stands at {settlement}, a town with no wall.
verdicts.finding: The landed same-page twin `Beasts & Monsters: frontier, force without a perimeter` opens its own [ledger] NUMBERED row - its index 0, the line a falsy seed draws - with 'At {settlement} the muster stands in an unwalled town': the same subject, the same verb, the same slot and the same two reads, differing only by the country clause the twin adds. The twin reads the same roster and prints beside this pool on every frontier town, so the reader meets one sentence twice. The refinement's own declared target (A) was exactly this distance, and it paid for it by trading the draft's 'an unwalled town' for the plainer 'a town with no wall' - a density trade that bought a distance it did not get.
verdicts.cure: Take the face off the twin's ledger subject-and-verb while keeping the appositive (the variant's only V1 grammar) and the ratified class word: e.g. 'A muster is entered at {settlement}, a town with no wall.' The curer re-spreads v1's four force-verbs if 'entered' then doubles with face 1. Add no claim; keep the slot exactly once; do not open on the slot.

verdicts.quote: The town's defense is people rather than works.
verdicts.finding: The shipped line standing VERBATIM under ADDENDUM 6 and Part B 21.4: lawful under the card (the CONTRAST names sibling pool keys of this row, R-DA-02 and wall 5, and is the opening move, closing nothing), both reads on one copula in eight words, the pool's short line (R-DA-05), and the pool's only instance of the shape. Smoothing it would be the regression the density law names.

verdicts.quote: This place is defended by its own force and by no wall.
verdicts.finding: The doubled by-phrase is a construction no sibling face uses; 'its' binds to the subject 'This place', which is the town, so W1's lawful direction holds; no mind, plan, saying, decision or capacity is given to the town (R-DA-14's FEELING non-move, W22, W23); no slot, as the parent carries none (ARCH 2.5).

verdicts.quote: What the town has under arms is people, and nothing built stands
verdicts.finding: The cleft is a construction no sibling face uses. 'nothing built stands about the place' is the negation of ENTAILMENT A-7's ratified generic for the wall class ('what the town has built'), localised by 'about the place' so it reads over the works and not over the town's fabric. The cleft's exhaustivity runs over the armed, not over persons, so it is not the refused totality column.

verdicts.law: Part B 21.4 the density law; and A11 / the same-page C7
verdicts.quote: make up the defense here, and the place has no perimeter
verdicts.finding: Two faults in one line. (i) DENSITY: the draft carried both reads on ONE verb with the absence riding attributively ('make up the defense of this unwalled town'); the refinement split it into two coordinate clauses with a joint. The law the refiner cited - 'unwalled' belongs to the landed twin - required dropping ONE WORD, not the compression, so the extra flattening has no law behind it, and it costs the variant its only V1 grammar member. (ii) SAME PAGE: the twin's own [street] variant carries 'People under arms stand here in frontier country', so this face repeats the twin's three-word opener and its deictic 'here', in the same angle, on the same page.
verdicts.cure: Restore the single-verb attributive so both reads ride one verb again, and move the opener off the twin's street row, adding no claim: e.g. 'A force under arms makes up the defense of this town, no wall standing about it.' Keep the variant slotless.

verdicts.quote: A stranger sees a force under arms at {settlement} and no line.
verdicts.finding: The shipped visitor frame kept at its compression with only the unlicensed member word replaced at the class grain - the variant's density floor. The stranger sees and does nothing else (W27: never acts, decides, is told, judges or takes a name). 'no line' is a wall word inside its own negation (REFERENT 2.1: walls-BODY in DS-DEF-2) and is this pool's own word on the page.

verdicts.quote: What a newcomer notices at {settlement} is a standing force
verdicts.finding: The cleft is its own construction and fronts what is met rather than who meets it. 'notices' is the block's own palette word for this angle ('what a stranger notices first, without being told'), so the salience the cleft carries belongs to the stance and is not a judgment the face adds (W27). Both reads stated; closes on a civic noun.

verdicts.law: A11 / the same-page C7; the skeleton's section 0 reading (d) word allocation
verdicts.quote: A traveller comes upon people under arms at {settlement}.
verdicts.finding: The landed twin's [visitor] variant holds all three of this face's load-bearing choices: 'a stranger comes upon armed people, and about the town finds nothing walled' and 'meets people under arms in a town with no wall'. This face takes the verb, the force noun and the wall word together, in the same angle, on the same page - and 'no wall' is the collocation the skeleton's own allocation ceded to the twin while this pool was given 'sees' and 'no line'.
verdicts.cure: Keep the two-sentence form and the thread ({settlement} carried forward as the second sentence's subject) and drop the two items the twin holds beside the verb: e.g. 'A traveller comes upon the town's force at {settlement}. The town shows no perimeter.' The curer re-spreads v3's four absence surfaces so none doubles inside the variant.

verdicts.quote: The force a stranger meets at {settlement} stands in a place
verdicts.finding: The force is the subject, the eye sits inside a reduced relative with no 'which' (R-DA-03), and the absence rides attributively - the variant's fourth construction and its V1 grammar member. The stranger meets and nothing more (W27); no use of the absent wall, no inference, no forecast, no count.

verdicts.law: the card's may NOT (a second fact, a future) + skeleton 0.6(b) no capability verdict + the block's fence (presence is standing, no recorded history); the ambiguity that opens a claim after the spine
verdicts.quote: {settlement} is entered with no wall and no force.
verdicts.finding: On the INVASION & WAR row the passive 'is entered' is the row's own event verb: a town that is entered is a town an army got into. The clause carries a second reading in which the two absences are why the entry succeeded, so the capacity verdict ('cannot be resisted here') and the history ('nothing has come') that the rewrite exists to drop return as an implicature on the CANONICAL-AT-ZERO line, the wording a falsy seed draws. The office's formula is lawful (R-vi/W7); this verb is not safe on this table.
verdicts.cure: Swap the verb for an office formula that cannot read as entry by force, keeping the nine-word shape and both limbs on one negated surface: '{settlement} is set down with no wall and no force.' (the register card's own word for what a clerk does; no record noun added, W24 intact).

verdicts.quote: For war, the town of {settlement} has no force and no works.
verdicts.finding: R1 at the class grain ('the works' is W15's always-safe spelling for any wall-class member; no member, no material, W11), R2 at the class grain, the frame fronted as the reading's standpoint (0.6(c)), the naming form (W5), the slot once and not opening the row (T-F8), one negated surface, the close on a civic noun the field names (R-DA-04).

verdicts.quote: Neither garrison nor militia is kept at {settlement}, and no wall stands.
verdicts.finding: R2 stated at the read's own decomposition (garrison and militia are the reader's two parameters, each inside its own negation, so W12's garrison bar is not engaged and no bucket is asserted present), R1 on the second clause. Also the pool's safest face against C7: on the 14 town-tier firings the required Town watch stands and this wording denies only the two buckets the key consults. The negated opener is the variant's one spend and is not an absence opener (R-ii/W10).

verdicts.quote: The town of {settlement} stands unwalled. Against organized aggression, the town keeps no muster.
verdicts.finding: R1 in its positive-condition form so no absence opens the face; R2 on 'the muster', the ratified class word that asserts no roll (ADDENDUM 13 A.5; OV-5); THE THREAD satisfied by the noun 'town' carried forward (R-i at k = 0); the frame is the shipped sentence's one licensed residue and is never an agent or given an outcome; the second sentence adds a licensed read rather than glossing the first (no MEANING move, R-DA-03/R-DA-12).

verdicts.quote: Against an army, {settlement} has neither wall nor force.
verdicts.finding: The frame fronted, the doubled negation bound to the two class nouns rather than to a bare 'nothing', the present tense, nine words against the shipped fourteen. The counterforce's thing-that-did-not-happen is the BUILDING and the KEEPING, stated flat: not the army's not coming (no history, W17/R-DA-19), not what would be stopped (no forecast, A2).

verdicts.quote: What {settlement} has for war is no wall and no muster.
verdicts.finding: The cleft is a genuine construction difference from its siblings (the subject is a free relative, not the town) and is built on what the town HAS, never on 'what stands against', so the chair's owed (iv) is not needed and the absent works are never made an agent that stands, opposes, bars or holds (R-iii). Claim-equal to its siblings (A6).

verdicts.quote: At {settlement} the town keeps no force and stands with no wall.
verdicts.finding: 'Keeps' is the engine's and the register's own verb for a force; the two-verb construction on one subject is carried by no other wording; the reads are reversed against the spine and the close moves to the wall (R-DA-04). Recorded, not failed: the locative slot and the generic subject name one thing twice in four words where W5's naming form exists for that job — a wobble, not a wall.

verdicts.quote: No muster is kept at {settlement} against a force in order.
verdicts.finding: The negated opener is variant 2's one spend; the second sentence ('The town is unwalled.') is POSITIVE, so no second negated sentence is created (R-ii/W10, wall 3), and at four words it is the register's short line (R-DA-05), which the pool otherwise lacks. THE THREAD: 'the town' is anaphoric on the proper name just set down, the subject does not change and nothing is handed off (1.4.1). Recorded for the chair: this is the pool's one second sentence carrying its predecessor's referent by anaphora rather than a repeated noun, and no lawful rewrite supplies the noun (the marker's owed (vii)).

verdicts.quote: The place has no wall about it and keeps no force.
verdicts.finding: 'The place' is 0.6(d)'s zero-risk spelling on the slotless variant; 'about it' is a locative adjunct on the ordinary sense of a town wall and keeps the class NOUN at 'wall', so D-6's bar on a geometric generic as the class word is respected; dropping the frame is the angle's right (0.6(c)). Recorded: 'about it' sits one step from the predicated encirclement that fails face 3, and a curer must not import it there a second time (A5 inside the variant).

verdicts.quote: Unwalled, the town keeps no force against an army.
verdicts.finding: Eight words carrying both limbs; R1 fronted in its positive-condition form so no absence opens the face; the frame LAST as the passage's one turn outward (THE THREAD); the town's own possessive idiom keeps the street stance legible without giving the town a mind (W22/W23).

verdicts.law: R-DA-19 and the block's fence (institution presence is a STANDING fact with no recorded history) + ENTAILMENT alias trap A-4 ('the muster' is the CLASS word; the word is four things and the ACT and the roll are not this read's); the ambiguity that opens a claim after the spine
verdicts.quote: the town is without a muster or a wall.
verdicts.finding: This is the pool's only INDEFINITE 'a muster'. The three lawful uses elsewhere ('keeps no muster', 'no wall and no muster', 'No muster is kept') force the body reading by their verb or their bareness; 'without A muster' makes the noun countable and admits the EVENT reading — the town has not held a muster — an act on a read that records no act, no history and (on every town this pool fires on, militia === false) no muster holder at all (0.5; W24). The marker barred attempt 2's 'musters no soldiers' for exactly this and the article reopens it. Secondary, recorded not ruled: this is also the thinnest of the four street faces ('the town is without' is the ledger's flat surface under the [street] tag) and it fronts the same frame word as variant 1 face 1.
verdicts.cure: Drop the article and let the two class words run bare, keeping the preposition-carried negation (the one thing that keeps this variant off a single coordinator) and the close on the wall: 'Against war, the town is without muster or wall.'

verdicts.law: ENTAILMENT D-6 / alias trap A-7 (continuity is NOT ENTAILED of the wall class; the class has no always-safe geometric generic) + the SKELETON RULE (R1 stated at its full width) + 21.4 read against the DRAFT
verdicts.quote: no wall rings the town.
verdicts.finding: 'Rings' PREDICATES a complete circuit. The read is walls === false — no member of the walls bucket stands, a bucket whose members include a Citadel (inner) and Gates (if walled) (a point), of which 'rings' is false even when they stand. So the face asserts only that nothing encircles the town, strictly weaker than R1: a reader cannot tell 'nothing is built' from 'something stands but does not encircle'. True on this pool's population and still a lost read. It is also a regression against the draft on the refiner's own named target: the draft's 'no wall stands about the place' carried the presence verb and the refinement traded it for an enclosure verb to win a concrete image (T1/T2).
verdicts.cure: Restore the presence verb without restoring the pool's third 'stands about': 'This town keeps no force, and no wall stands.' (nine words, both limbs, the close still on a civic noun; no claim added, none lost).

readAloud: Variant 1: three of the four read clean and unhurried, and face 3's two sentences breathe — the short standing clause first, the frame carrying the second. The canonical line is the one that catches: read aloud on a page headed Invasion & War, '{settlement} is entered...' lands for a beat as something an army did, and the ear has to go back for the ledger.

Variant 2: the tightest of the three to the ear, and the only one with a short line — face 3's four-word close lands where it should. The audible blemish is face 2, where the place is named twice inside four words ('At {settlement} the town...'); nothing is untrue, but a reader hears the seam.

Variant 3: the town's own talk is clearly audible in 'The place has no wall about it' and in 'This town', and almost inaudible in 'the town is without', which reads in the ledger's voice under the street's tag. 'Rings' is the one verb in the pool that draws a picture, and it draws the wrong picture — a circuit that is not what the record holds.

verdicts.quote: Neither a court to try a charge nor

No record noun, no person, no cause, no totality; closes on the slot, a name, not a pronoun (R-DA-04); hands a court and a place of confinement forward to the one modifier k allows.

verdicts.law: skeleton 0.7 (c) TOTALITY over the read; the card's may NOT: a second fact; CLERK-LAWS C2 (a same-page claim the engine's own record contradicts)
verdicts.quote: What stands at {settlement} against a wrong done inside the town
verdicts.finding: The specificational pseudo-cleft is EXHAUSTIVE: it equates everything that stands at {settlement} against an internal wrong with the two absences, so the face asserts that NOTHING stands against a wrong done here. That is the same over-reach the drafter itself refused in 'nowhere to take it' and 'no legal machinery' (draft section 2, judgment 2), and on every tier this pool fires on the governing row carries a recorded Dispute mediation / Community mediation service (skeleton 0.4, open row 3) — unread by this card and therefore undeniable. The frame may state the two absences AGAINST the row's matter; it may not make the matter a totality.
verdicts.cure: Drop the exhaustive frame and keep the matter as an adjunct: 'Against a wrong done inside the town {settlement} keeps no court to try it, and no cell.' — same claim set, same reads, same order, no cleft.

verdicts.law: W3 (the band marker) and W5 read against CLERK-LAWS C2 / the head record on the same page; skeleton 0.4 (CONFIRMED) and open row 6
verdicts.quote: The town of {settlement} is entered with no gaol
verdicts.finding: The appositive naming form PREDICATES the band: it says {settlement} is a town. This pool fires on EVERY thorp, hamlet and village and on NO town or city (skeleton 0.4, confirmed against institutionalCatalog.js and the two flags: a town's required hall always sets hasCourtSystem), so the page's own head record reads a tier below town on every firing and the face contradicts it. The bare generic subject 'the town' is ruled to carry no tier value (0.7 (d)) and is untouched by this finding; 'the town of X' is the one spelling that states the band. Ruling-dependent: the marker's open row 6 is unruled and W5 ratifies the naming form for a settlement that IS a town, so the chair can convert this.
verdicts.cure: Drop the band word, keep the formula, the slot and the read order: 'The place, {settlement}, is entered with no gaol to hold under an offence and no court to try the offence.'

verdicts.quote: are what {settlement} does without
verdicts.finding: The positive frame carries the compound lack with no negating operator at all; 'does without' is a ratified present-move verb for a body's absence (skeleton 0.8); 'the one it names' is the row's matter at layer NONE in OBJECT position, never a subject, an agent or a decider (W22); closes on a condition, a fourth close kind for the variant (R-DA-04); the slot is not sentence-initial (T-F8).
verdicts.cure: (no cure)

verdicts.quote: A wrong done here comes before no court
verdicts.finding: The marker's own licensed street realisation (skeleton section 2 (4), verbatim): the wrong is a generic hypothetical of the frame in the habitual present, not an event that happened (R-DST-B), and both reads stand as one keyed condition with no {settlement} on a slotless variant (ARCH 2.5). The second limb is re-seated on the body ('no cell is kept'), so no person is a subject — the one law fault the refinement was called to fix. Closes on a name.
verdicts.cure: (no cure)

verdicts.quote: Here the town keeps no court against a quarrel
verdicts.finding: Twelve words: the pool's relief line, which the register card and R-DA-05 want in the street and which the shipped row's short line held. Both reads stand (the gapped 'and no gaol' carries the prison read on the ratified class word, A-17); 'keeps' is a ratified possessor verb and never a fused agent (W23: the town keeps, it does not settle, judge or hear); the deictic and the street's own matter noun carry the stance, so it is not an inventory line.
verdicts.cure: (no cure)

verdicts.law: A5 / the four-faces rule and W4's construction contract (a sibling paraphrase past a synonym swap)
verdicts.quote: For a wrong done here this town keeps no court
verdicts.finding: It is face 1's construction with the words changed: the same SUBJECT (the town), the same READ ORDER (court then prison), the same verb phrase ('keeps no court'), the same gapped second limb landing on a bare prison class word. The three things the rule makes the faces differ in — the subject, the order of the reads, the landing noun — are all shared; what differs is the fronted adjunct's length and two synonyms ('against a quarrel' to 'to try it'; 'no gaol' to 'no place of confinement'). The refinement's own spread claim that no two faces of one variant share a subject, a read order and a landing noun (refine section 3) does not hold on this pair.
verdicts.cure: Re-seat the face on a different subject and reverse the read order, keeping the claim set: 'In this town no place of confinement stands for a wrong done here, and no court to try it.'

verdicts.law: the [street] stance grain (the street states the standing plainly) read against the cross-variant echo of v1's row construction; A11's echo bound
verdicts.quote: Neither the court a charge would come before nor the cell
verdicts.finding: Two grounds, neither proven. (a) The angle: a twenty-word correlative carrying two embedded subjunctive relatives is the clerk's syntax rather than the town's plain statement of its own condition; the deictic close ('stands in this town') and the plain standing verb argue the other way, and unclarity alone is not a finding. (b) The echo: this is v1 face 0's skeleton at one remove — Neither [court + its charge relation] nor [prison + its hold-under relation] + a standing verb + the place — so a reader drawn v1 face 0 and then v2 face 3 meets one sentence twice; the within-variant four-faces rule does not reach across variants and no ratified law names cross-variant construction echo. Recorded for the chair rather than failed.
verdicts.cure: If the chair rules: spend one of the two subjunctives — 'Neither the court a charge would come before nor the cell that holds under it stands in this town.'

verdicts.quote: A stranger who comes to {settlement} with a complaint finds
verdicts.finding: The stance is carried by arrival and a perception verb alone: the stranger comes, finds, and does nothing else — it is never wronged (the shipped event, dropped), never told, never surprised, never named (W27; product scope). 'with a complaint' is the frame's matter in the standing form the marker licenses ('a stranger with a wrong to bring', skeleton 0.8), not an event that happened. Both reads, the slot once and not sentence-initial, the person periphrasis in object position (W22), a matter close.
verdicts.cure: (no cure)

verdicts.quote: The court a stranger would look for at {settlement}
verdicts.finding: The definite is bound by the subjunctive relative and then denied, which is A-16's safe direction (the noun names the sought thing, the predicate denies its standing); the inverted ellipsis gives the pool its one such construction and the variant a fourth close kind; 'would look for' is the edge and never a future indicative (A2); no frame noun is needed, the frame being the angle's and never the floor's (skeleton 0.7 (c)).
verdicts.cure: (no cure)

verdicts.law: the ambiguity that opens an unlicensed reading after the spine (R-DA-18, costume in the syntax); the card's may NOT: a standpoint
verdicts.quote: no cell stands for the one a charge names
verdicts.finding: 'stands for' is a fixed English idiom — it represents, or it tolerates ('will not stand for it'). Read alone, which is how the seeded roll delivers it, the face offers the reader 'no cell represents the one a charge names' and, at the idiom's other sense, a prohibition-flavoured verdict on the accused. The pool's own diction primes 'stands' as the standing verb only for a reader who has already met the other faces, and no face may lean on a sibling it will not be drawn beside. This is the same fault the refinement itself failed in the draft's 'has a place in this town' (refine section 1, v2 c), applied consistently.
verdicts.cure: Take the idiom off the verb without touching the claim: 'To a stranger at {settlement} no cell is kept for the one a charge names, and no court for the charge.'

verdicts.law: R-DA-11 (no intent or feeling for a collective thing) and W23 / the D-F16-D-F18 pattern, reached through the ambiguity of the noun; the card's may NOT: a standpoint
verdicts.quote: the town's want of a court
verdicts.finding: 'want' carries the absence sense the face intends and the DESIRE sense it does not, and the possessive seats the desire on the town: read alone, the face says the town wishes it had a court and a place of confinement. That is a feeling predicated of a collective — no field carries motive, belief or mood on this card, and the town is the record's subject, never an agent that hopes. The antique air is meant to live in the noun (R-DA-18), but not in a noun whose second sense adds a claim.
verdicts.cure: Keep the possessor and the compound lack, drop the ambiguous noun: 'What a stranger sees at {settlement} is the town without a court and without a place of confinement.'

readAloud: v1 — Read aloud, the variant is the strongest of the three in the ear: face 0's correlative lands on the name, and face 3's positive frame ('are what {settlement} does without') is the one line in the pool with no negation in it at all and the one that sounds least like a form. The two failures sit in the same place, the middle: face 1 and face 3 are both wh-clefts, one basic and one inverted, which the refinement's tic count did not register as a pair, and face 1's cleft is what tips its frame into the totality. Curing face 1 as named removes the cleft and the pair together. Face 2's gaol-first order is worth keeping through its cure: it is the variant's only reversal.

v2 — The street reads as the town would say it only in its first two faces; face 1 is the best line in the pool to the ear (twelve words, the gapped 'and no gaol' landing on four syllables) and face 0's frame-first opening is the marker's own. The back half of the variant is where the ear goes flat: face 2 says face 1 again at greater length, and face 3 changes register entirely into a clerk's correlative. Curing face 2 as named restores the variant's spread without adding a word of claim; face 3 is left to the chair.

v3 — The stranger is handled well throughout: it comes, looks, finds and sees, and it is never wronged, told or surprised, which is the whole of what the shipped row got wrong. The variant's two failures are both single words doing unintended work — 'stands for' and 'want' — and both cures are one-phrase swaps that leave the reads, the order, the landing and the word counts where they are. Face 2 and face 0 share the cell-then-court order and a matter close; after the cure they still differ in subject and noun, but the variant's read-order spread is its thinnest margin.

1. `[ledger]` — read aloud, face 0 is the pool's line: `and so does a place of confinement` lands because the ellipsis makes the reader supply the formula. Face 3's short line lands too. Face 1 is face 0 said again more slowly, and face 2 trips on `is entered` — the ear hears a door before it hears a register.

2. `[street]` — the family reads as one movement (what is done, where it goes, what can be done with the person) and that movement is the variant's whole appeal; it is also exactly the claim the card refuses. Read aloud, the four faces are the most natural English in the pool and the least licensed prose in it, which is worth the chair seeing stated that plainly.

3. `[visitor]` — the four openings are genuinely four (finds / What a stranger finds / To a stranger / On arrival) and the eye stays an eye throughout. Face 2's `stands … stands` is the one flat beat in the variant; face 3's second sentence is the quietest close in the pool and the best argument for the two-sentence shape.

verdicts.quote: The town's law at {settlement} stands entered, and so does
verdicts.finding: Both reads stated as standing facts of the record; the ellipsis carries the office's own formula onto the second read at no claim cost; the ledger cites nothing; lands on a carriable civic noun. The pool's compression, and the density floor the refinement rightly kept verbatim.

verdicts.law: the owner's four-faces rule (A5: a face is never its sibling's construction with the vocabulary swapped); W4 the construction contract
verdicts.quote: In the town of {settlement} the law is entered
verdicts.finding: Face 0's construction with two substitutions. Subject is the court read's own noun in both; read order court→prison in both; one coordinated sentence in both. Only the fronted locative and the second clause's surface move, so two of the three discriminators the owner names (subject · read order · landing noun) are identical. The draft had declared this face's subject as THE TOWN; the refinement moved it onto its sibling's subject, which W4 calls the regression. The bare `the law`, possessor-less, is also one notch off the referent table's ratified surface for this read (REFERENT-TABLE.draft.md:58 gives the function word as "the town's law").

(W1-clean, the possessive follows `the town`; R-vi's own formula; court→prison kept; lands on a condition, so the close-kind still varies against face 0.)

verdicts.law: the card's `may NOT: … a second fact`, reached through the ambiguity that opens a claim after the spine; the owner's stand-alone rule (an unweighted roll picks the face, so every face stands alone)
verdicts.quote: A place where a person can be held is entered at
verdicts.finding: The ledger's entering formula is put on a PLACE noun, where `is entered` carries its spatial sense first: read cold, the sentence says a place of confinement is walked into at {settlement} — an act, and a second fact no field holds. Face 0 escapes this because its subject is an abstraction and its verb is `stands entered`; here the subject is a place and the verb is the bare passive. The face cannot be rescued by its siblings, because the composer never renders them together.

The law that town keeps is entered." (No record noun is introduced — `on the roll` stays barred by W24 on a SOURCE-UNRESOLVED read — and the construction, subject and read order are untouched.)

verdicts.quote: People can be held at {settlement}; the town's law stands entered
verdicts.finding: Both reads; D-16's own patient wording, so no person acts (W22); the semicolon is the pool's only one (0.083 against R-DA-06's 0.130); subject, read order and landing all differ from face 0; the court read keeps the ratified possessor.

verdicts.law: ADDENDUM 13 part A item 6 on D-15 (a CONDITIONAL used without its condition resolved on THIS town's record); W14 the label bar; the card's `may NOT: … a second fact`
verdicts.quote: A thing done wrong at {settlement} goes to the town's law
verdicts.finding: `goes to the town's law` is the process claim, not the standing. D-15's ENTAILS column holds ONE entry for the court flag and it is conditional — "a process that runs", with "a dispute GOES BEFORE a magistrate" as its own worked example, licensed only where a `Courthouse` row stands or the Town hall's `Dispute arbitration` service is instantiated. This pool resolves neither (the key reads the bare flag, which L-16 sets off a required town hall on every generated town and city). W14 states the trap in one line: a civil arbitration is recorded, a criminal trial is not — and beside a place of confinement, "a thing done wrong" reads criminal. Naming the destination does not resolve the condition; it only fixes the destination noun. The skeleton's §2(6) licence for "goes somewhere … with the somewhere named" contradicts its own §2(3), which calls the same clause UNLICENSED, and the card decides against it.
verdicts.cure: Keep the shipped frame — it is the variant's declared construction and its density floor — but make its predicate a licensed read, so nothing travels and nothing runs: "Where a wrong is done at {settlement}, the town's law stands, and the town keeps a place of confinement." The offence becomes the face's occasion; the two claims are the two standings.

verdicts.law: as face 0 (D-15 CONDITIONAL unresolved, ADDENDUM 13 A.6; W14 the label bar)
verdicts.quote: a wrong done there goes to the town's law

verdicts.law: W14 the label bar; D-15 CONDITIONAL unresolved (ADDENDUM 13 A.6)
verdicts.quote: the town has its law to hand for a wrong done there
verdicts.finding: Softer than "goes to" but the same reading: the purpose phrase asserts that the town's law is applicable to WRONGS, which is the criminal sense of a flag the engine sets from a meeting hall. The rest of the face is sound — two sentences, the thread carried by `that town` off `the town`, W1 clean.

verdicts.law: W14; D-15 CONDITIONAL unresolved; R-DA-04 (land on the civic noun the field names); W15 / REFERENT-TABLE.draft.md:58
verdicts.quote: the town has law to hand for what is done wrong there
verdicts.finding: Three things at once. The purpose phrase is face 2's breach in a third dress. The face then CLOSES on `what is done wrong there` — the offence, which is no civic noun the card's fields name, so the spine hands a following modifier a noun the block cannot license (THE THREAD; R-DA-04). And `has law to hand`, article-less, makes the court read a mass noun where the ratified surface is the possessed function word.

verdicts.quote: finds the town's law standing, and finds a place where
verdicts.finding: Both reads; the stranger only comes and finds, never brings, asks, is given or is named (W27); `finds … standing` puts the perception on a STATE and so stays clear of R-DA-11's sense-verb-on-an-abstraction; `who comes` is a who-relative, not a which-tail; lands on a condition. The variant's longest line and its strongest beat.

verdicts.quote: What a stranger finds standing at {settlement} is a place where
verdicts.finding: A pseudo-cleft, not an expletive opener (R-DA-07 reaches `There is` / `It is`), and the block's landed siblings use the same shape. Read order flips to prison→court against face 0, the subject is the finding itself, the landing is the court read's own noun. `standing` sits inside the cleft, so both conjuncts are found as states.

verdicts.quote: To a stranger at {settlement} the town's law stands, and a
verdicts.finding: The dative of perspective was tested against the card's `may NOT: a standpoint` and does not reach it: the skeleton reads that bar as a standpoint on the office's CONDUCT, and this face evaluates nothing — it states what stands to a newcomer, which skeleton §3(5) licenses in those words. The construction is also the block's own (`To a stranger the country around {settlement} is quiet …`, the `settled, defenses beyond the need` sibling at the dock tip). Both reads; subject and landing differ from every sibling. The doubled `stands` is a read-aloud matter, not a law.

verdicts.quote: On arrival at {settlement} a stranger finds a place of confinement
verdicts.finding: Both reads; the second sentence carries `that town` forward from the slot (R-i; the demonstrative has a real antecedent, unlike the sibling pool's failed `That muster`), and the shift of subject is the passage's turn and sits last, as THE THREAD requires. The stranger sees and does nothing else.

readAloud: Variant 1 [ledger]: read aloud the four land flat and entered, which is the angle's own sound; the ear does not stumble until the two participles. 'a person held' and 'for keeping that person' are exactly where a listener starts picturing somebody already in the cells, and they are the two faces this round fails. Face 2's 'are carried as standing' is the one place the office's own voice is audible, and it is worth keeping for that even though the phrase reads stiffly on the cells.

Variant 2 [visitor]: 'A stranger at {settlement}' and 'A traveller at {settlement}' land alike to the ear, one after the other, and the doubled 'sees' in the second is the only figure in it; a listener hears the same sentence twice. The contrast face is the best-sounding of the four, because the eye arrives, meets a thing, and then meets the lack of one, in that order.

Variant 3 [street]: the strongest-sounding variant of the three and the one a table would repeat. 'put a person away' and 'no court says what for' are the town's own words, and the four faces each stop on a different word (what for, that person, a court, a say), so nothing rings twice.

verdicts.quote: A person can be held at {settlement} and brought before no court.
verdicts.finding: Both reads stated: (P) the modal capacity to confine, (L) the court-bound lack. Not an inventory line — 'brought before no court' is the court's own idiom negated in place, a turn and not the flat restatement skeleton §1.6 names. The ledger stance holds: the fact set down flat as standing, nothing measured, nothing cited. No record noun (W24), no person as agent (W22), no body the read does not reach (W20); one bracketed tag, the slot once, not as the opener (T-F8).

verdicts.law: the card's `may NOT` (a fact the record does not hold) · ADDENDUM 13 A item 1 and the entailment table's D-16 NOT ENTAILED (anyone currently held) · skeleton §4.3's named hazard 'those held' · W6 the doubled beat
verdicts.quote: no court sits to try a person held
verdicts.finding: The face leaves the modal frame in its second clause. 'can hold people' is a capacity; 'a person held' is a reduced relative with no modal over it and asserts that a person IS held — an occupancy the hasPrison flag never records (the flag spans roster rows; capacity, conditions, sentences and anyone currently held are all NOT ENTAILED). It is also the same read twice inside one sentence (hold → held), the summarising beat W6 bars. Its passing siblings keep every person noun under a modal ('can keep a person, and no court can try that person'), so the defect is this face's and not the pool's.
verdicts.cure: Cut the participle and keep the clause court-bound: '…, and no court sits to hear a charge.' The charge is the absent court's own function-object, asserts nothing of this town, and moves the close off the absence onto an object. No claim added; the shipped turn 'can hold people' is untouched.

verdicts.quote: Cells at {settlement} are carried as standing, and the town keeps no court.
